title: Temptations (MSX) commented disassembly
reason: Approved repository-root addition with substantive primary-source evidence. Commented disassembly/reassembly of native MSX Temptations and tape-loader modules. Generated listings, address-anchored commentary and supporting tools form one subject root. openMSX is a validation aid, not a modern gameplay wrapper. Substantial annotated Z80 reconstruction with upstream byte-match reports and actual verification scripts; semantics remain partly unresolved.

title: Netwalk — Amstrad CPC native puzzle game
reason: Approved new repository-root addition with substantive primary implementation evidence. A new native Z80 implementation of the Netwalk puzzle, with growing-tree maze generation, animated tile rotation, connectivity/completion logic, menus and timer. It is homebrew game code rather than a recovered commercial Netwalk binary. Upstream publishes a playable CPC puzzle game; loading screen, high scores, sound effects and original music remain unfinished.

title: CommandoJS — rough first-level C64 Commando browser remake
reason: Accepted at the reviewed scope. Native CoffeeScript/MelonJS reimplementation of the C64 Commando subject. Hero, enemy, weapon and application code implement gameplay. This browser implementation is distinct from the tracked C64/Spectrum disassemblies and Amiga arcade conversion. rough first-level implementation. Cakefile lists and builds CoffeeScript application sources, but a recipe and QUnit tests do not establish successful compilation or execution. README limits the game to a rough first level, unoptimized code and incomplete tests. No build or demo was exercised; all build flags remain null. Rights: MIT.

title: B.A.T. II — recovered original Atari ST game sources
reason: Approved repository-level candidate with substantive primary implementation evidence. Original Computer’s Dream/Ubi Soft Atari ST source preservation, not a new disassembly or engine rewrite. Retain original source copyright notices; no root license or blanket redistribution/commercial-use grant was found. Recovery completeness remains open. The README describes an attempt to recover 1992 source from floppies. BATII.S is substantial original code, but a complete modern recipe, required includes/data and successful rebuilt output have not been established. All build flags, including byte equality and current playability, remain null.

title: c64-re-tools — agent-oriented C64 engineering toolkit
reason: Accepted at the reviewed scope. General-purpose C64 reverse-engineering/development tooling. The MCP controls a stock VICE process; this is neither a game reconstruction nor a game-specific emulator wrapper. Live VICE/Ghidra tests are opt-in and skip when prerequisites are absent; no build or tool execution performed. README npx installation claims not independently verified against package registry.

title: Dungeon Master Codex
reason: Approved repository-root addition with substantive primary-source evidence. TypeScript/React Three Fiber reimplementation/remaster using extracted original maps/tables and source references. Concrete movement and FUSE code implement rules directly without a guest CPU interpreter. Upstream-reported v0.9.4 public browser build in late stabilization, with completed endgame playtesting reported upstream.

title: Shoot to Move — Amstrad CPC native game source
reason: Substantial native source for the reviewed homebrew game; canonical root not already tracked. The Android export material is ancillary packaging of the retro game. It is not evidence of a native Android gameplay rewrite, so Android is not added as a native target.

title: LOLAN — preserved CPC native-code Forth-like compiler and games
reason: Approved repository-level candidate with substantive primary implementation evidence. Richard Brooksby’s original Forth-like compiler, utilities, Pede and Tron lightbikes form one archive/tool record. The README mentions a future LOLAN 2 recovery but no separate archive was inspected or counted. Source license is unclear; original binary-format compiler source is only partly decoded. The author states that everything still runs in a CPC464 emulator and gives commands for LOLANC.BIN and Pede, so runnable=true is an attributed report about preserved disk binaries. This does not prove current source compilability, completed compiler-source decoding, or any byte-exact rebuild. Compiler-wide playability is not asserted.

title: Roadwar 2000 — C64 disassembly and TypeScript rewrite
reason: Accepted at the reviewed scope. Native TypeScript gameplay reimplementation plus the substantial Python rwtool extraction/decompilation toolkit. Reviewed mainp.ts implements game-state arithmetic directly; the game does not execute original 6510 instructions. Needs generated font.json; clean clone is not self-contained for runtime. TODO retains play-testing and balance questions; byte-exact fixture claims do not establish whole-game parity. Original disk images and decoded game data are in tree; no root licence located.

title: AIPong
reason: Explicit introduction-to-coding workshop example; retain as a teaching reference, not a substantial standalone game in this batch. README explicitly describes a simple Pong game for the Amiga Ireland Blitz Basic tutorial; source header identifies the January 2018 workshop. The complete small source loads background/paddle/14 ball images, builds a 320x256 five-bitplane display, reads joystick and arrow-key paddle inputs, accelerates/bounces the ball, checks paddle collision and increments scores. Only two November 2023 commits are present in the inspected history page, initial commit and source/assets upload. Inspected commit 07277fd4d3ca812ecd2a77521fa80ed81dab3ade; actual root tree 1b16b1655bdf6bb5e9f5901a2ea0a1a23935d8a3.

title: Georg Rottensteiner Common library — lineage reference
reason: Directly compiled shared dependency and format evidence for Painter; not an independent new application record. Recursive tree contains 1,564 entries spanning graphics/UI, filesystem, codecs, networking, rendering and third-party support rather than a focused C64 program. FormatIFF.cpp implements IFF ILBM header/palette/bitplane loading plus saving; FormatIFF.h declares FORM/ILBM/BMHD/CMAP/BODY and auxiliary chunk identifiers. Painter's project file directly references this repository-shaped P:\Common hierarchy, including Grafik\ImageFormate\FormatIFF.cpp. No root README, root license text or independent build project was found in the complete tree; the verified consumer is Painter. No repository-wide license grant was established. Third-party libraries and source notices must remain separately attributed. CAMG handling is skipped, so special Amiga display-mode support cannot be inferred from generic IFF handling. Broad host portability and build completeness were not validated; no direct C64-specific format implementation was established. License: No root LICENSE/README grant found; no license assigned to repository as a whole.

title: VS64 Developer Tools bundle — lineage reference
reason: Binary-package manifest for the already tracked VS64 development environment, not a new tool implementation. The complete tree has README/LICENSE/packages.json plus ZIP packages; no assembler/emulator implementation is present. packages.json lists Windows ACME, Exomizer, VICE, JRE, Oscar64, LLVM-MOS, cc65, X16 emulator and Denise, a macOS ACME package, generic KickAssembler, and an empty Linux section. README documents jdeps/jlink construction of a Java runtime for KickAssembler; LICENSE.md explicitly calls this a collection of binary packages. ZIP contents were not unpacked or executed; listed package names and versions are manifest evidence, not verified functioning toolchains. Component-specific licenses differ; KickAssembler is explicitly described as Unknown/Freeware. The bundle's GPL/Zlib/Apache/BSD/PSF listings do not make one repository-wide license. Some distributed tools also target Commander X16, Amiga or other machines; that does not create additional projects for this packaging root. License: LICENSE.md is a component inventory, not a uniform grant: GPL-2.0, GPL-3.0, Zlib, Apache-2.0-with-LLVM-exception, BSD-2-Clause, PSF-2.0, JRE Classpath exception, and KickAssembler unknown/freeware.

title: YAM — Yet Another Mailer

title: PC98Emu — C# NEC PC-98 emulator

title: XEngine — native Pascal DOS game toolkit

title: Atalanta

title: Wondersnake — WonderSwan Color snake game

title: PC98Bridge — PC-98 serial inspection and file-transfer agent

Gameplay runs at a different speed on BBC hardware according to the author; preserve the Electron target rather than treating the related BBC implementation as the same machine build.

title: AmiFTP 2 — restored native Amiga FTP client
reason: README documents GUI transfers, Aminet mode, ARexx scripting, transfer resume and PASV/PORT support; ftp.c implements socket connection, command/reply, send/receive and passive fallback paths. The SAS/C smakefile links ReAction, rtasl.lib and tcp.lib with the UI/FTP implementation; AS225 support is disabled in the current documented version. README requires AmigaOS 3.2 with ReAction; older ClassAct systems are only described as possible. External SDK/toolchain assignments and link libraries must be supplied. No secure-FTP/TLS functionality or security audit is established by this review. Top-level MIT terms do not erase the legacy four-clause Berkeley notice retained in ftp.c.

Existing decision markyturtle-ttedisbuilder-netcore-port excludes a .NET Core port as separate lineage. Source invokes shrinkler.exe, salvador.exe, zopfli.exe and optional other packers; tool availability is not verified. No explicit project-wide license in tree; bootblock/data and compressor rights are separate. No image boot, loader interoperability or output checksum test performed.

title: wav2amiga — ProTracker sample preparation
reason: MainForm.cs resamples via NAudio MediaFoundation, extracts the high byte of 16-bit PCM and writes raw sample files.
